hints.title: Prefix Branching with Wildcard Matching
hints.text: A dictionary must support word insertion and pattern search where the dot character matches any single character. How can a prefix tree structure branching options?

hints.title: Recursive Search on Wildcard Encounter
hints.text: Standard characters navigate directly to the matching child node. When a dot character appears, branch across all available child nodes in the current dictionary node.

hints.title: Depth-First Branch Exploration
hints.text: Define a helper function dfs(node, index). If index reaches word length, return whether node marks a terminal word. If character is a dot, iterate over all node children and return true if any path succeeds.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.time: O(M) for add, O(26^M) worst-case for search with dots
complexity.notes: addWord is linear in word length. Search without dots is O(M); search with dots explores candidate branches.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Scanning a flat list of words with regular expressions costs O(N * M) per query and times out on 10,000 queries.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Common prefixes share internal nodes, conserving memory across large vocabularies.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Clean recursive backtracking for wildcard exploration and terminal word boundary tracking.
